hierarchy.note: Used only in major codes (Civil Code, Penal Code, Commercial Code). الكتاب الأول, الكتاب الثاني.
Intermediate level found in the Penal Code between Kitab and Fasl. Not present in all codes. القسم الأول, القسم الثاني.
Primary structural grouping in most laws. الباب الأول, الباب الثاني. May appear at top level (without Kitab) or within a Kitab/Qism.

Higher division ABOVE the article basic unit. الفصل الأول, الفصل الثاني. Bluebell workaround: use DIVISION keyword; post-process to rename <division> → <section> in AKN output. Same pattern as Egyptian profile.
THE basic unit. Numbered continuously throughout the entire law regardless of Kitab/Bab/Fasl boundaries. مادة (N). Insertion: مكرراً (bis) suffix → art_5bis.
Paragraph break within an article. May be unlabelled (cited positionally) or explicitly numbered (1)(2)(3) or (أولاً)(ثانياً). Detect numbering style from document.
Numbered list items: (1)(2)(3) or (أ)(ب)(ج). Normalise Arabic-script numerals and Abjad letters to Western Arabic/Latin for eId construction.

decree_law.label: Presidential Decree (مرسوم جمهوري)
decree_law.note: Presidential decrees and Revolutionary Command Council (RCC) decree-laws from the pre-2003 era. Structurally identical to ordinary laws. Distinguished by enacting formula and FRBR subtype 'decree-law'. RCC-era decrees (1968–2003) use revolutionaryCommandCouncil TLC.

regulation.label: Executive Regulation (نظام / تعليمات)
regulation.note: Executive regulations (نظام) and ministerial instructions (تعليمات) subsidiary to a parent law. Published in Al-Waqā'i' al-'Irāqiyah.

cpa_order.label: CPA Order (أمر السلطة المؤقتة)

hierarchy.note: CPA Orders are in English and use Anglophone section-based structure, not Arabic article structure.

cpa_order.note: Coalition Provisional Authority Orders, Regulations, Memoranda (May 2003 – June 2004). English-language documents. Anglophone section-based hierarchy. Many remain in force per TAL Art. 26 unless expressly repealed.

hierarchy.note: 2005 Constitution has 6 Chapters (Abwab). الباب الأول: المبادئ الأساسية, الباب الثاني: الحقوق والحريات, etc.
Same DIVISION workaround as for acts.
144 Articles in the 2005 Constitution, numbered continuously.

frbr.note: Law number and year taken from citation رقم [N] لسنة [YYYY]. Arabic-script numerals (٠-٩) must be normalised to Western Arabic (0-9) for URI construction. CPA Orders have no year in the URI — numbered sequentially from 1. KRG legislation uses iq-ku sub-national code.

structuring.prompt_additions: Arabic and Kurdish RTL text. Basic unit is ARTICLE (مادة/Maddah), not SECTION. Hierarchy for major codes: BOOK > [PART >] CHAPTER > [DIVISION for فصل/Fasl] > ARTICLE. Simple laws: [CHAPTER >] ARTICLE only. No SUBSECTION level — use PARAGRAPH for فقرة/Faqra and POINT for بند/Band. Article numbers are continuous throughout the entire law regardless of higher divisions. Use ASCII Bluebell keywords (BOOK, PART, CHAPTER, DIVISION, ARTICLE, PARAGRAPH, POINT) but preserve Arabic article content verbatim. Arabic-script numerals ٠-٩ should be normalised to 0-9 in structural position markers only. Insertion articles: مادة 5 مكرراً → ARTICLE 5bis. CPA Orders use English section-based structure — use SECTION/SUBSECTION/PARAGRAPH hierarchy instead, with structure_iq_cpa.txt variant.

supranational_memberships.note: Founding member (1945). No direct-effect supranational legal instruments. Conventions require ratification and domestic enabling legislation.

direct_effect_exceptions: Security Council Chapter VII resolutions — binding on member states

display.note: Arabic RTL primary display. Article numbers may appear in Arabic-script numerals (٥) or Western Arabic (5); pipeline normalises to Western Arabic for eIds. Kurdish Sorani also uses Perso-Arabic script (RTL). Review UI must set direction: rtl; unicode-bidi: embed.
